cleanIntro: The 21A Bobcat is a tip-up: the barrel lever releases the barrel and it swings up, so the chamber is right there to see and reach — no racking a slide to check it. ⛔ The strip is done with the hammer FULLY COCKED and the safety OFF, which is the opposite of most pistols and the reason people think theirs is broken when it will not come apart.

steps.title: Magazine out, then tip the barrel and LOOK
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out. Then push the barrel lever forward to release the barrel — it swings up and the chamber is exposed. On a tip-up this is the easiest chamber check in shooting; there is no reason to skip it.
steps.aside: Release Barrel by pushing the barrel lever forward.
steps.quote: Remove Magazine by depressing the magazine release button.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY (Field Stripping of Unloaded Pistol)

steps.title: Barrel forward to a SOLID stop
steps.action: Swing the barrel forward over its hinge until it reaches a solid stop — further than the normal loading position. That extra travel is what clears the hinge so the slide can come off.
steps.quote: Swing the Barrel forward over its hinge to solid stop.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY (Field Stripping of Unloaded Pistol)

steps.title: ⛔ Hammer FULLY COCKED, safety OFF
steps.action: This is the step that catches people. The strip is done with the hammer fully cocked and the safety off — not decocked, not on safe. Prove the chamber empty first, then cock it.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY (Field Stripping of Unloaded Pistol)

steps.title: ⛔ Slide back an EIGHTH of an inch, lift the front, listen
steps.action: Grip the front of the slide between thumb and index finger, retract it about one eighth of an inch, and lift the FRONT of the slide above the frame's barrel hinge. A click tells you the recoil spring levers have let go of the slide. Wait for that click — pulling the slide further back without it is fighting the springs, not releasing them. Then run the slide forward until it clears the frame's guide lugs.
steps.aside: and pull the slide forward until it clears the frame's guide lugs.
steps.quote: Retract the slide about one eighth of an inch—lift the front end of the slide above the frame's barrel hinge
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — DISASSEMBLY (Field Stripping of Unloaded Pistol)

steps.title: Grips stay ON for a normal clean — strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, magazine. The grips only come off if the pistol is exceptionally dirty, and Beretta says plainly that they are not needed for normal cleaning. ⛔ Nothing further is recommended, and with the slide off the hammer must never be dropped by pulling the trigger.
steps.aside: Only if exceptionally dirty will it be necessary to remove the grips.
steps.quote: It is not necessary to remove grips for normal cleaning.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — FIELD STRIPPING

steps.title: Clean it when residue has ACCUMULATED — and use CLP
steps.action: Beretta's trigger for cleaning is not a round count but a condition: clean the pistol whenever a notable amount of powder residue, grease, cartridge metal particles or field dirt has built up in the action. A good grade of CLP is the recommended product.
steps.aside: Use a good grade of CLP (Cleaner-Lubricant-Preservative) gun oil.
steps.quote: Clean pistol whenever a notable amount of gun powder residue, grease, cartridge metal particles, field dirt, etc. have accumulated in the action.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CLEANING

steps.title: ⛔ Soft tools only — never a sharp instrument
steps.action: Lint-free cloth, a small brush, pipe cleaners, cotton swabs, toothpicks and a small wooden applicator. ⛔ Never a sharp instrument: on a small pistol the parts you would be scraping are the ones that have to stay square, and a gouge in a breech face is permanent.
steps.aside: Use a lintfree cloth, a small brush, pipe cleaners, cotton swabs, toothpicks and a small wood applicator to remove dirt, etc.
steps.quote: DO NOT use a sharp instrument.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CLEANING

steps.title: ⛔ Bore from the CHAMBER end, always
steps.action: Clean the barrel bore and chamber thoroughly after every session with a rod and a patch, or a brush fitting tightly — and always work from the chamber. The barrel is off the gun for this, which is the whole advantage of a tip-up.
steps.aside: Always clean the barrel bore and chamber thoroughly after shooting using a cleaning rod with a patch, or brush fitting
steps.quote: clean the barrel from the chamber.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CLEANING

steps.title: ⛔ Re-check the barrel days later for SWEAT-OUT
steps.action: ⛔ This one is specific to the 21A's book and it is easy to miss. A few days after you have cleaned it, look down the barrel again: oil and solvent trapped in the steel can SWEAT OUT and leave the bore wet or, worse, corroding under a film you thought was protective. It costs ten seconds and it is the difference between a stored pistol and a pitted one.
steps.quote: Be sure to recheck the barrel for possi- ble sweat-out a few days after the shooting cleaning.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CLEANING

steps.title: Breech face, firing pin CHECK, then a light oil
steps.action: Always clean the breech or bolt face of the slide, and then check the firing pin moves freely — that is a function check, not a cosmetic one, and it is the one thing on this pistol worth proving before it goes back in a pocket. Oil the moving parts lightly and rub a thin film over the exterior for rust protection.
steps.aside: For most effective exterior rust protection, rub a thin film of oil onto the surface with a cloth.
steps.quote: Be sure to check for free movement of the firing pin.
steps.cite: Beretta Model 21A User Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — CLEANING

deepAbsentReason: Beretta stops the owner at the field strip on this pistol and prints it in capitals: "CAUTION!! Further Disassembly not recommended for cleaning." The grip-panel removal is published and rides as a cleaning note rather than a deeper strip, and it is explicitly for an exceptionally dirty gun only. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else — including from the 30X/20X successor book in this repo, which describes a later gun.

Cleaned thoroughly after every shooting session

⛔ Firing pin proved to move freely

cleaning.name: GRIPS
tasks: Off only if the pistol is exceptionally dirty; screws snug, never forced

reassembly: Grips back on first if they came off — screws snug, ⛔ never forced.
Front of the slide elevated, rear placed over the frame just in front of the guide lugs.
Slide rails pulled back over the guide lugs while the front is lowered gently onto the recoil spring levers, then moved forward to stop against the barrel hinge ears.
⛔ Thumb across the front of the slide's sidewalls, PRESS DOWN — sharp clicks mean the recoil spring levers have engaged the slide cutouts.
Underside of the slide checked flat against the frame — slide and frame parallel.
Barrel swung closed and the barrel lever checked closed.
fncheck: Reassembled: press down across the front of the slide's sidewalls until you hear SHARP CLICKS — that is the recoil spring levers engaging the slide cutouts, and without it the pistol is not assembled. Check by eye that the underside of the slide sits flat on the frame's sliding surface, slide and frame parallel. Swing the barrel closed and check the barrel lever closes. ⛔ Then confirm the firing pin still moves freely before the pistol is carried.
